title: Nghỉ chăm con cho cha · Problems / Solutions
prompt: Some societies are considering reserving part of paid parental leave exclusively for fathers. What problems could this create, and what measures could be taken to address them?
instructions: Give reasons for your answer and include any relevant examples from your own knowledge or experience. Write at least 250 words.

grammar.name: Động từ tình thái chỉ khả năng
grammar.example: Low replacement pay can make leave unusable for families dependent on the higher earner's income.
grammar.why: Trong câu “Low replacement pay can make leave unusable for families dependent on the higher earner's income.”, cụm “can” đặt hệ quả ở mức khả năng thay vì khẳng định chắc chắn. Phần nghỉ không chuyển nhượng tạo thời gian để cha tự thực hành chăm con, thay vì mẹ dùng hết. Cơ chế thay đổi phân công qua trải nghiệm và quyền lợi riêng, không chỉ khuyên cha tham gia.

grammar.name: Giới hạn bằng without
grammar.example: Employers should publish return-to-work arrangements before leave begins, allowing fathers to take responsibility for care without having to negotiate continued employment from a vulnerable position after their absence.
grammar.why: Trong câu “Employers should publish return-to-work arrangements before leave begins, allowing fathers to take responsibility for care without having to negotiate continued employment from a vulnerable position after their absence.”, cụm “without” liên kết hai ý ngay trong câu được chọn; phải giữ đúng quan hệ nghĩa khi rút gọn. Không lấy quyền trên giấy làm bằng chứng sử dụng thực tế. Nếu lương thay thế thấp và cha là người kiếm chính, mất thu nhập có thể làm gia đình không chọn nghỉ.

paragraphs: Reserved parental leave concerns who actually performs care, rather than simply how many weeks a family receives. Reserved leave may go unused when families cannot absorb lost earnings; adequate replacement pay and job protection must therefore accompany the entitlement.

Low replacement pay can make leave unusable for families dependent on the higher earner's income. An entitlement paid well below normal earnings can be unusable where the father supplies most household income. Families may preserve the mother's larger share of care simply because they cannot absorb the loss, leaving the reserved weeks formally available but largely untaken. Reserving leave changes incentives only if fathers can afford to take it and do not face a credible risk of losing employment or promotion opportunities. The distributional problem is particularly serious for a household with little savings, because even a short reduction in earnings can threaten rent and essential bills. If wealthier fathers take leave while poorer fathers cannot, a formally equal entitlement may widen differences in who gains practical caregiving experience.

Pay levels and employment protection should make the entitlement financially realistic. Adequate pay and job protection must accompany non-transferability, because a formally individual entitlement has little effect when household finances make using it unrealistic. Employers should publish return-to-work arrangements before leave begins, allowing fathers to take responsibility for care without having to negotiate continued employment from a vulnerable position after their absence. A replacement rate that protects lower earnings, combined with clear protection against dismissal, would reduce the immediate household cost and the longer-term career risk that deter participation.
Overall, the policy should be assessed by uptake across income groups and changes in everyday care, rather than by the nominal number of weeks reserved for fathers.

paragraphs.quote: Pay levels and employment protection should make the entitlement financially realistic. Adequate pay and job protection must accompany non-transferability, because a formally individual entitlement has little effect when household finances make using it unrealistic. Employers should publish return-to-work arrangements before leave begins, allowing fathers to take responsibility for care without having to negotiate continued employment from a vulnerable position after their absence. A replacement rate that protects lower earnings, combined with clear protection against dismissal, would reduce the immediate household cost and the longer-term career risk that deter participation.
